messages:

Subject: Recap: Context-window fit & truncation concerns / next steps

Hi Jena / Marco —

Thanks again for the demo today. Quick recap + proposed next steps so we’re aligned: 

What you described
- Primary workload: clinical encounter ingestion + multi-section summarization for care teams. Average note length ~18k tokens, 10–15% of records spike >40k tokens.
- Key constraints: no lossy truncation on findings/diagnoses, HIPAA-compliant handling (VPC/private deployment), and predictable latency for in-chart retrieval (SLO ~800ms p50 when fetching summaries).
- Current pain: existing models chop context, summaries miss critical meds/allergies, and hallucination on lab values.

Redwood fit / recommendation summary- For initial eval: run a two-track experiment: 1) long-context models with native 32k+ KV support; 2) sliding-window + overlap + synthetic prompt stitching for heavier tails.
- Candidate models to test (we’ll manage variants & quant configs): RW-Long-35B (32k context quantized), RW-Large-13B-Long (8k native + stitched KV), and an ensemble run with a high-precision 70B snapshot for critical mentions.
- Evaluation focus: truncation boundary behavior, summarization fidelity on ood/instrumented notes, hallucination rate for numeric fields, and per-summary token cost.

Deliverables / timeline proposed- By Feb 16: Share sample prompt sets + prompt-engineering notes and a benchmark summary (small, reproducible corpus of 200 notes with ground-truth highlights).- By Feb 20: Run initial long-context pass on 50 records (Redwood hosted sandbox) and share results + latency/cost matrix.
- Follow-up week of Feb 23: demo results, propose pilot configuration (Dedicated or Private depending on compliance).

What we need from you- Upload 200 redacted notes to the shared Drive folder (link below) or give us s3 read access. Mark 1–2 canonical notes where truncation caused loss of critical information.

Attachments: notewise-context-eval-plan.pdf (plan + metrics), prompt-sets-v2.json (starter prompts)
Links: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-eval-notewise (please add access)

Next steps- Jena: can you confirm you’ll drop the sample set by EOD Feb 14?
- We’ll schedule the results demo the week of Feb 23 once initial pass completes.

Thanks —

Camila —

Thanks for the clear recap and timeline. We can prepare the sample set; two clarifications before we upload: 
1) Data format — should notes be single JSONL per note or full CDA XML? We can provide both but want to match your eval harness.
2) Hallucination checks — we’ll include gold-labels for findings/meds where possible, but for older notes we only have clinician highlights. Will that be sufficient for your fidelity metrics?

Also concerned about the stitching approach (sliding-window). In prior trials, stitching introduced duplication and inconsistent summarization across sections (the model repeated the problem list). Can you include an experiment that measures redundancy and preserves the single-source-of-truth?

We expect to add the sample set by Feb 14 but may push to Feb 15 if legal needs to re-redact one appendix.

Camila / Marissa —

Quick internal notes to shape the sandbox run: 
- Format: prefer JSONL (id, text, meta) for fastest ingestion to our eval pipeline. If they provide CDA XML we’ll write a parser but ask for JSONL if possible.
- Eval plan highlights (what we will measure): truncation point behavior (where key entities drop), summary recall@k for gold highlights, hallucination rate (numeric & medication assertions), redundancy score (n-gram overlap between windows), end-to-end latency (p50/p95), and cost per summary token.
- Stitching options: (A) hierarchical summarization (section-level summaries + final synthesis); (B) overlapping sliding windows with dedupe heuristics; (C) KV cache + retrieval of section anchors for critical fields (fastest route but requires structural parsing). We should run A + C in parallel and compare.
- Compute / capacity ask: initial 50-record pass can run on 1 dedicated GPU small pool; if we do 70B snapshot runs we’ll need a larger instance — plan to surface costs in the benchmark spreadsheet.

I attached a brief benchmark-summary.csv template and the prompt-sets-v2.json we discussed. Camila: can you share these with Jena and request the JSONL preference?

Hi Jena / Marco —

Great questions — thanks. Short answers and next steps: 

1) Preferred format: JSONL is ideal. If you can also include a small sample of CDA for edge-case parsing that’s helpful.
2) Labels: clinician highlights will work for the initial fidelity metrics. For numeric fields we’ll annotate a subset manually if you can mark ~30 canonical encounters.
3) Redundancy/duplication: we’ll instrument the runs with a redundancy metric and include the hierarchical A vs sliding-window C comparison. Our hypothesis: hierarchical + anchor retrieval reduces duplication while keeping critical fields intact — we’ll validate.

I’ve shared three artifacts in Drive and attached the plan + prompt set in this thread. If legal needs an additional redaction pass, Feb 15 is fine.

Proposed immediate next steps: 
- Jena: upload JSONL (or give s3 read) by Feb 15 EOD.
- We’ll run the 50-record pass Feb 17–18 and share results Feb 20.
- Demo bookable for Feb 24 (morning PT) — I’ll send a calendar invite once we confirm.

DocuSign / procurement note: If pilot needs Dedicated capacity, I’ll loop in our procurement lead and prep a short SOW for a 30-day pilot.

Thanks again — looking forward to the run.
